items.text: Starting in January 2027, ai_forecast version 2 will be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. ai_forecast version 2 uses a foundation model for more accurate time series forecasts in SQL, and adds holidays, external covariates, and non-negative forecasts. Queries that don't specify a version continue to use version 1.

items.title: Genie One enhancements
items.text: Push notifications on Android (Public Preview): The Genie mobile app now sends push notifications on Android for long-running prompts and scheduled tasks. See Push notifications. Voice input in Genie One: Voice input is now generally available in Genie One on the web, in the desktop app, and in the mobile app. You can dictate prompts, and voice input transcribes your speech into text. Voice input is available in US and EU regions. Workspace skills and skills from other folders: Genie One now lists workspace skills and skills from other folders that you register in Genie Code. You can't edit these skills in Genie One. See Workspace skills and skills from other folders.

items.title: New VARIANT manipulation functions
items.text: The following SQL functions for manipulating VARIANT values are now available in Databricks SQL and Databricks Runtime 19 and above: variant_insert: Inserts a new object field or array element at the specified path. variant_set: Inserts or replaces an object field or array element at the specified path. variant_delete: Removes object fields or array elements at the specified paths. variant_array_append: Appends a value to the array at the specified path. variant_pick: Returns a VARIANT containing only the specified paths, preserving their parent structure. variant_strip_nulls: Recursively removes variant null fields from objects and, optionally, variant null elements from arrays. Error-tolerant versions are also available: try_variant_insert, try_variant_set, and try_variant_array_append. See Built-in functions.

items.title: On-demand billing for Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.text: Sections: Only pay for what you consume; What's different; Two capacity models, one platform; What changes when you turn it on; Control how much compute each workspace can use; Give every team a lane; How it behaves in practice; Monitoring what's actually happening; How to estimate your on-demand bill (quick method); Getting started; The one line to remember; Next steps. Many warehouse workloads are highly variable. In some cases, a few peak periods demand significant compute, while the rest of the month usage is much lower. Shared capacity is a great fit for steady, predictable workloads, while workloads with variable or intermittent demand can benefit from a consumption-based model. On-demand billing for Fabric Data Warehouse gives you that flexibility: you can use dedicated compute when your warehouse needs it and pay for the compute you consume. items.title: Fabric on-demand billing and Zero-provisioned (F0) Capacity (Preview)
items.text: Sections: Flexible capacity models; How on-demand billing works; Example usage scenario; Spend controls and governance; Monitoring on-demand consumption; Why this matters; Learn more. Microsoft is introducing a new way to consume Fabric called on-demand billing. This includes a new F0 SKU, enabling customers to get started with zero upfront commitment, as well as a hybrid option that pairs any traditional F SKU with the flexibility of on-demand billing. In addition to the traditional Fabric capacity model, customers can selectively enable on-demand billing for individual Fabric workloads, such as Data Factory or Data Warehouse, which are broken down into what is known as on-demand billing categories. Customers can set usage thresholds per billing category to maintain predictable governance and spend controls.
